mechanism_narrative: The sharp drop in WORKPLACES at t-0w reflects a near-term loss of weekday foot traffic that will spill into retail and recreation within two to four weeks, lowering RETAIL_REC as commuter-linked shopping and dining trips weaken.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -16.3 to -44.3 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the prior four-week mean after a WORKPLACES drop of more than 20 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM above 25 points signals substitution toward essential errands and home-based routines, which suppresses discretionary retail visits over the next one to two weeks and pushes RETAIL_REC lower.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 25 points for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached 31.0 at t-1w and remained 30.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to fall within two weeks after GROCERY_PHARM remains above 25 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES move down together, the shared reduction in travel and commuting reduces incidental shopping trips, producing a lower RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -20.6 to -26.0 while WORKPLACES fell from -16.3 to -44.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite simultaneous weakness in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: An upward break in RESIDENTIAL mobility above 13 points indicates more time spent at home, which reduces discretionary retail outings and drives RETAIL_REC lower within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week after RESIDENTIAL crosses above 13 points.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains below -25 while WORKPLACES is also below -30, the combined mobility restraint implies a restrictive operating regime that suppresses discretionary retail demand and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -26.0 and WORKPLACES was -44.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform its prior four-week mean when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A four-week climb in PARKS mobility reflects a shift toward outdoor leisure, which substitutes for indoor retail and recreation and lowers RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -26.4 at t-1w to -19.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite a sustained rise in PARKS mobility.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM rises while TRANSIT falls, people are concentrating on essential, local trips and avoiding discretionary travel; that combination suppresses retail-and-recreation visits for about two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above 30 while TRANSIT remains below -20
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 30.0 and TRANSIT was -26.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks when high grocery/pharmacy mobility coincides with weak transit mobility.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS combined with stable or improving TRANSIT signals resumed out-of-home leisure circulation, which should lift retail footfall and raise RETAIL_REC over the next one to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases for 2 consecutive weeks while TRANSIT does not worsen
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -26.4 to -19.6 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its prior four-week average after two weeks of improving PARKS with non-deteriorating TRANSIT.
